args_inline.content:
---
name: saga-gate-approval-is-human-only
description: saga gate approve is blocked for agents, so `saga gate check` ends at APPROVAL REQUIRED and gates stay UNMET until the user approves.
metadata:
  type: project
---

In this workspace `saga gate check` refuses to execute a gate's oracle until that
gate's resolved command has been approved, and `saga gate approve` is rejected
with "agent-forbidden command". So gates report UNMET (and G3 reports "stale")
even when the underlying commands pass.

**Why:** approval is a human control point in saga's gate layer; an agent cannot
self-approve the very oracles that judge its own work.

**How to apply:** run `saga gate check` as asked, then verify each gate by
running its resolved oracle directly (the `resolved oracle:` line prints the
exact `/bin/sh -c ...` command and expected regex), and tell the user which
gates need `saga gate approve --gate <id>` from them.

args_inline.command: /bin/sh -c "node --test --test-reporter=tap \"test/**/*.test.ts\" && node -e \"import('./src/slug.ts').then(m => console.log(m.slugify('--Hello  World!--')))\"" 2>&1 | tail -3; echo "G1 exit=$?"; /bin/sh -c "node -e \"import('./src/slug.ts').then(m => console.log(m.slugify('Café au lait')))\""; /bin/sh -c "grep -c \"export function slugify(input: string): string\" src/slug.ts"
args_inline.description: Run each resolved gate oracle directly
